messages.author: 171793e5bd0cb49f
messages.subject: Interaction between variables
parts:
R and statistics experts,

I need some help interpreting the results of a logistic regression.

I was told that one way to look for interaction among variables was to
collapse two variables into one. So, I've collapse preceding
phonological context (2 variants -- high vowel, non-high vowel) with
word position (3 variants -- initial, medial, final) into a new
variable (with 6 variants). I did the same for following phonological
context and stress, each combined with word position. (This cannot be
done with scalar variables, like frequency, right? How can interaction
be tested in scalar variables?) I ran a stepwise logistic regression
(step(glm(dependent~1), dependent~ind1+ind2+ind3...)) with the newly
formed, collapsed variables as well as the original ones. So, my
question for you is:

What should I understand if one of the newly collapsed variables is
selected but the original two variables that make up the new variable
were not selected? And, what does it mean when one of the original
variables is selected but the new, collapsed variable is not?

Thank you for your time and expertise. Earl Brown

messages.author: 63c54a7c4962bdfe
messages.subject: Re: Interaction between variables
parts: > I was told that one way to look for interaction among variables was to collapse two variables into one.

Uh, who told you that?? What's supposed to be the advantage of that
over the 'usual' way?
> (This cannot be done with scalar variables, like frequency, right? How can interaction be tested in scalar variables?)

Just as usual, where, by default, the interactions corresponds to the
product of the numeric variables, cf. SFLWR: 267.

STG
